rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the highest-value first experiment is to establish a simple, well-understood baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal configuration: no image processing, no aggregation, no fusion, and PCA is a standard, low-risk encoder. This gives a clean reference accuracy for the RNA modality alone. Subsequent experiments can then isolate the marginal contribution of (a) adding image modality, (b) switching to learned RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt), (c) multiprofile + aggregation, and (d) fusion strategy. Starting from the simplest configuration also minimizes confounding variables and failure modes, making it the best uncertainty-reducing choice under a tight 10-experiment budget.

We have only one data point (config_001: RNA-only, single-profile, PCA → 48.5% acc), so the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries useful signal for this task at all. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is a clean, single-variable comparison to config_001: same profile setting (single), same architectural simplicity (no aggregation/fusion), differing only in modality. This isolates the effect of switching from RNA to image features. If image accuracy is comparable or higher, it strongly motivates multimodal fusion experiments later; if it is much lower, it suggests RNA is the dominant signal and we should prioritize RNA encoder/aggregation improvements. This is the highest-information next step because it calibrates the value of the image modality before committing budget to more complex multimodal configurations, and it avoids changing multiple design axes simultaneously.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA, single profile, PCA n2000) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while config_010 (Image, ResNet50) is very weak at 20.8%, indicating RNA is the dominant signal source. Uncertainty: PCA is a simple linear projection; a pretrained foundation model like scgpt may capture richer biological structure (cell-type programs, gene regulatory context) that PCA misses. This experiment (config_007: RNA, single profile, scgpt) isolates the effect of the RNA encoder while keeping profile setting identical to config_001, so any accuracy difference is attributable to the encoder choice. This is the best use of experiment 3 because: (1) it directly tests whether the current 48.5% ceiling is due to a weak encoder, (2) it provides a stronger or comparable RNA baseline before investing remaining budget in multiprofile aggregation or multimodal fusion, and (3) it avoids changing multiple variables simultaneously, preserving interpretability for the 7 remaining experiments.

Evidence: PCA n2000 single-profile RNA (config_001, acc=0.485) is the best configuration so far, clearly outperforming scGPT single-profile (0.411) and image-only ResNet50 (0.208). The image modality appears weak, so the primary direction for improvement is likely within the RNA pipeline. Question: Does multiprofile aggregation (avgpool) improve upon the best single-profile RNA encoder? config_002 is a minimal single-variable extension of config_001—same encoder (PCA n2000), same modality (RNA only), but adding multiprofile with the simplest aggregation (avgpool). This cleanly isolates the effect of multiprofile without confounding changes to encoder or fusion. Why this is the best next step: With 6 experiments remaining, establishing whether multiprofile helps the strongest RNA encoder before investing in multimodal fusion or more complex aggregators (transformer) is the most information-efficient move. If avgpool helps, we can then test transformer; if not, we can pivot to scVI or multimodal with confidence that the single-profile ceiling is well-characterized.

The strongest result so far is config_002 (RNA-only, multi-profile, PCA_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 acc, a +10.6 point jump over its single-profile counterpart (config_001, 0.485). This confirms multi-profile aggregation is highly beneficial. The key open question is whether transformer aggregation can further improve over simple avgpool. config_003 changes only the aggregation method (avgpool → transformer) while holding RNA encoder (PCA_n2000) and profile setting (multi-profile) fixed, giving a clean isolated comparison. Resolving this before moving to multimodal settings is critical: if transformer aggregation helps, it will inform which aggregation to pair with fusion in later multimodal experiments; if it does not, we can focus remaining budget on fusion strategy and image encoder selection rather than aggregation complexity. With 5 experiments left, this single-variable test maximizes information gain about a design axis that directly impacts the best current configuration.

The strongest result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 accuracy, showing that multiprofile + avgpool is a highly effective combination. The image-only baseline (resnet50) was very weak (0.208), and scgpt single-profile (0.411) underperformed pca_n2000 single-profile (0.485), suggesting encoder choice matters. scvi_n200 is the only RNA encoder not yet tested in any setting. Config_005 isolates the encoder variable by swapping pca_n2000 → scvi_n200 while keeping the proven-best multiprofile + avgpool configuration. This tells us whether a learned latent encoder (scvi) can surpass a linear PCA projection in the multiprofile regime, which directly informs whether further encoder exploration is worthwhile or whether we should pivot to multimodal fusion with the best encoder. With 4 experiments remaining after this one, establishing the best RNA backbone before testing multimodal combinations is the highest-information use of this slot.

1) Evidence: The best configuration so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc. The RNA-only space is well-characterized: multiprofile > singleprofile, avgpool > transformer, and scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 > scgpt. Image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.208), but we have zero multimodal evidence. 2) This experiment tests whether adding resnet50 image features via concat fusion to the best-known RNA setup (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) provides any complementary signal beyond the RNA modality alone. It is the minimal multimodal extension—only the model setting and image component change, while all RNA-side settings remain at their validated best. 3) With only 3 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information single step: if multimodal helps, we gain a new direction to exploit (e.g., ViT-L or weighted fusion) in the last 3 slots; if it does not, we confirm RNA-only is the ceiling and can spend remaining budget on fine-grained RNA-only refinements. It avoids changing multiple variables at once and directly addresses the largest unexplored design axis.

The best result so far is RNA-only scvi_n200/multiprofile/avgpool (config_005, acc=0.650). The only multimodal test (config_030: scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + concat) scored 0.632, slightly *below* the RNA-only baseline, suggesting resnet50 image features add noise rather than signal. The critical remaining question is whether a substantially stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) can make multimodal fusion actually surpass the RNA-only ceiling. config_036 isolates exactly this: it keeps the proven-best RNA pipeline (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) and concat fusion, and swaps only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l. If ViT-L lifts accuracy above 0.650, the final experiment can explore weighted fusion or transformer aggregation on top; if not, we confirm RNA-only is the best strategy and can spend the last budget on a fine-grained RNA-only variant. This single-variable change is the highest-information experiment available given 2 slots remain.

The current best is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.715020. Evidence strongly supports this configuration family: scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 for RNA encoding, imagenet_vit_l >> resnet50 for image encoding, multiprofile+avgpool > transformer for aggregation. The one untested variable within this best family is the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted). Config_037 isolates exactly this single change, testing whether weighted fusion can further improve upon concat. This is the highest-value experiment because it directly exploits the strongest evidence while testing the most likely remaining source of improvement, and with only 1 experiment left after this, a targeted exploitation of the best-known direction is preferable to broader exploration.

The best result so far is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 accuracy. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder, multiprofile over singleprofile, imagenet_vit_l over resnet50, and concat over weighted fusion. The one remaining untested variable within this best-performing family is the aggregation method: we have only tested avgpool (0.715) but not transformer. In RNA-only settings, avgpool outperformed transformer (0.591 vs 0.519 for pca_n2000), but the interaction between transformer aggregation and the stronger multimodal fusion (scvi + ViT-L) is unexplored. As the final experiment, config_038 (same as config_036 but with transformer aggregation) is the most direct exploitation of the best configuration, isolating the aggregation effect in the multimodal regime. If it underperforms, it confirms avgpool is optimal and config_036 stands as the final best; if it surpasses 0.715, we gain a new best. No other untested configuration has a stronger prior probability of exceeding 0.715.
